subject: lavaanGUI in the Cloud prototype available for beta users

messages.author: 601aa4bb4d2fbfcf
messages.subject: lavaanGUI in the Cloud prototype available for beta users
parts:
Dean Lim and Geoffrey Hubona have created a novel (beta) and no-cost application we call "lavaanGUI in the Cloud." The beta prototype of the app, which came out of production today, allows you to run your lavaan analyses over the Internet using just a browser from any computer. You do not need to have R installed on your local machine, but you will need either: (1) a lavaan text (string) model object and a data file: or (2) a lavaan text (string) model object and a covariance matrix. I have a few samples files of each to provide that I have attached

If you are interested in using the no-cost beta app, go to http://pls-gui.com and get yourself a user name and then access the 'lavaanGUI in the Cloud' application by pointing your browser to http://pls-gui.com/lavaangui

Of course, we want to hear about application features and functionalities that do not work.

Geoff Hubona

messages.subject: Re: lavaanGUI in the Cloud prototype available for beta users
parts: No, you are mistaken about PLS-GUI, it is a separate application from lavaanGUI. PLS-GUI is original code and functions. Now I cannot say the same about  lavaanGUI, but I will have to defer to Dean on that one.

messages.author: 601aa4bb4d2fbfcf
messages.subject: Re: lavaanGUI in the Cloud prototype available for beta users
parts: No, they are two separate applications....lavaanGUI uses the sem(), cfa() and growth() functions straight from the lavaan package....if you look at the form, you will see that all of the arguments map directly back into those three functions as defined in the Lavaan package. That is why the estimation is the same, if I understand your question correctly. The lavaanGUI app, which is really just a prototype, just sits on the same server with PLS-GUI. At any rate, I'd be happy to give you the source code for the version that I have, which I have always given away freely to anyone who asks for it.
